title: POC scoping: cost modeling with Sapphire Systems
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on cost model and unit economics for a real-time summarization product. Discussed tokens per request, target latency, batching/caching knobs, dedicated vs hosted, benchmark plan and success criteria. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark with synthetic and production traces; Redwood to share pricing and a benchmark spreadsheet.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining; we'll run about 45 minutes today, scope the POC and agree next steps. Um Maya and I from Redwood, Evan, Priya, Liam from Sapphire?
[00:08] Evan: Yep that's us, thanks Jordan.
[01:02] Maya: Quick agenda: we want to understand your volume (qps), tokens per request, latency SLOs, data residency, and any compliance blockers. Then we'll map to cost model and POC plan. Sound good?
[01:18] Priya: Sounds great. Our product is a live meeting summarizer embedded in their CRM, so typical request is full meeting to concise summary, sometimes 1-2 follow ups. Avg meeting length 30 mins but we stream interim summaries too.
[01:45] Liam: Infrastructure note - all our infra in AWS eu-west-1, we need VPC peering for private deploys and strict KMS usage.
[02:10] Jordan: Cool. So to get into numbers - can you ballpark concurrent users and requests per day?
[02:26] Evan: Peak concurrent roughly 1200 users, but only about 8% use summaries in real-time so say 100 qps at peak. Daily active around 50k summaries.
[03:01] Maya: Great. Tokens per request? Full meeting transcript is ~10k tokens, but we chunk and call the model for summarization; effective tokens per API call around 1,200 on average. Some calls hit 2k tokens.
[03:33] Priya: Right, we chunk into sliding windows to keep latency low.
[04:00] Jordan: Okay, so ballpark unit economics: with 1,200 tokens per call and 100 qps peak - batching and caching changes this a lot. If you do no batching hosted calls at 1,200 tokens, per-token price x model matters. Our hosted pricing for the m-xxx-2k style model is $0.0006 per token served (note: placeholder) which would be...
[04:40] Evan: Wait can you repeat that per-token? I think we saw different numbers in the deck.
[04:48] Jordan: Sorry, rough numbers: for the curated open models we list 0.0004-0.0009 / 1k tokens depending on context, but let me be explicit: if it's $0.0006 per token that is $0.72 per request at 1,200 tokens. At 50k requests/day that's $36k/day which is obviously too high; so this is why batching, KV caching, and quantized dedicated runs matter.
[05:30] Priya: That math seems off - are you using per-1k or per-token? We charge per token in thousands, usually price is per 1k tokens.
[05:42] Maya: Sorry, yes Redwood prices shown are per 1k tokens - missed the unit. So $0.0006 per 1k tokens is $0.0000006 per token. Let's clarify: for a 1,200 token call, cost = 1.2 * $0.0006 = $0.00072 per call (hosted). So 50k calls/day -> $36/day.
[06:20] Evan: That is much more reasonable. Good cleanup.
[06:40] Jordan: Thank you Maya for the catch. So main levers: 1) batch size (we can batch many small calls to amortize kernel launch), 2) KV prefix caching to avoid re-encoding repeated content (meeting context), 3) quantized dedicated instances which drop model op cost.
[07:05] Liam: For us, latency SLO is 700ms for 75th percentile summary generation. We need 95th p to be under 1.5s.
[07:25] Maya: Understood. That's tight for long-context calls. Two approaches: use smaller context model with smart retrieval + streaming; or use dedicated high-memory GPUs with optimized kernels.
[07:50] Priya: For POC success criteria: 1) quality (ROUGE/ human eval score threshold we'll set), 2) latency under 1s p75, 3) cost target < $0.02 per summary, 4) integration feasibility into our VPC.
[08:20] Jordan: Those are good measurable goals. We'll propose benchmark configs to test those.
[09:00] Evan: Can you walk through an example cost calc with batching?
[09:12] Maya: Sure. Example: if you can batch 10 requests into one forward pass that shares prefix encodings, effective tokens processed reduces; plus continuous batching can increase GPU utilization. For 1,200 token avg full call, batching by 10 doesn't reduce tokens per user but reduces per-request overhead. If kernel amortization equals 30% of per-call cost, batching by 10 could cut that overhead to 3% per call. So a hosted per-call from $0.00072 becomes like $0.0005. Combined with caching (if 30% of tokens reused), effective token billing could be 840 tokens -> cost ~0.0005 * 0.84 = $0.00042 per call (numbers illustrative).
[10:10] Priya: We care most about bottom-line cost per summary at scale. Target < $0.02 seems wide - is that realistic?
[10:25] Jordan: For many deployments, yes. If you run dedicated quantized models at say equivalent $X/hour GPU and you reach high utilization, COGS per token falls dramatically. We can run numbers: e.g., A6000 equivalent throughput for our quantized runtime yields ~Y tokens/sec; amortize infra and infra cost, support, etc.
[11:00] Liam: Can Redwood run a synthetic benchmark using our trace so we can see delta between hosted and dedicated?
[11:12] Jordan: Absolutely. For the POC we typically run a 2-week benchmark: week 1 synthetic (replayed traces) on our hosted infra and a dedicated config; week 2 run production shadow traffic or a sampled trace on dedicated in your VPC if approved. We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet.
[11:38] Maya: We'll need a sample trace (anonymized) with token-level timestamps and request ids to replay. Also your target concurrency patterns.
[11:48] Evan: We can provide a 48-hour trace extract within a week.
[11:55] Priya: On compliance - SOC2 and ISO are required, and we need KMS/HSM integration with customer-managed keys for private deploy. Does Redwood support that?
[12:08] Jordan: Yes; Private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM and audit logs. Hosted supports encryption at rest but not customer keys by default. We'll share security docs.
[12:28] Priya: Also need to know data retention options and whether transcripts are stored.
[12:35] Maya: By default ephemeral logs kept 30 days; for Private you control retention and logs. We'll include retention and purge options in the security pack.
[12:50] Evan: Back to unit economics: what's the rough break-even point where dedicated becomes cheaper than hosted?
[13:00] Maya: It depends on utilization. Rough rule: if sustained utilization > 40-50% of a dedicated cluster and you have predictable throughput, dedicated often wins. If spiky with low baseline and many small customers, hosted is better. We'll include a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet.
[13:30] Liam: What about model variants for fallbacks? If primary model has outage, can we route to a smaller model automatically?
[13:42] Jordan: Yes, smart routing and fallback are built in; we can do canary and automatic downgrades. But model size and quantization changes affect quality; we'll capture quality deltas in the benchmark.
[14:05] Priya: Timelines - we want a POC in 6 weeks: week 0-1 planning, week 2 benchmark on hosted, week 3 spin up dedicated in our VPC, week 4-5 production shadowing, week 6 decision. Is that realistic?
[14:24] Jordan: That's aggressive but doable if we get traces and VPC access quickly. SE time required for custom instrumenting the trace.
[14:40] Evan: What are required Redwood artifacts for legal/procurement?
[14:46] Jordan: We'll share SOC2, ISO attestation, DPA draft, pricing sheet and an SOW for the POC.
[15:00] Maya: One more technical point: KV cache savings in summarization are high when you have repeated phrases or meeting templates. In our tests we saw 25-40% token reduction for repetitive enterprise meetings. But it's workload dependent.
[15:25] Priya: Good. For success criteria around quality: we'll define automated evals (ROUGE, BERTscore) plus a 50-sample human review where at least 80% pass.
[15:40] Jordan: Great. So immediate next steps: (1) Redwood sends benchmark spreadsheet and pricing by Tue, (2) Sapphire provides 48-hr anonymized trace by next Fri, (3) schedule kick-off for POC and VPC network review next week.
[16:05] Evan: Agreed. One question: competitor comparisons - do you have numbers vs Anthropic or OpenAI for same workload?
[16:18] Maya: We don't publish exact vendor price parity, but we can include comparative estimates and show how batching/caching yields different effective prices vs blackbox APIs. We'll add competitor notes.
[16:35] Liam: Any blockers from our side? We need security team approval for VPC peering and a PO for sensitive infra.
[16:45] Jordan: Understood. We'll include a procurement checklist.
[17:00] Priya: Can Redwood run an initial qual benchmark with 10% of traffic to validate quality before doing full 2-week run?
[17:10] Jordan: Yes - we can do a short smoke test once we have traces.
[17:28] Evan: Thanks all.
[17:35] Jordan: Thanks team; we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and docs.
[17:50] Maya: Bye.
[18:00] [call ends]
